facts: Germany resented the territorial losses and reparations imposed by the 1919 Treaty of Versailles.
Adolf Hitler began rearming Germany in the mid-1930s in direct violation of international treaties.
Imperial Japan invaded Manchuria in 1931 and launched a full war against China in 1937.
Britain and France conceded Czechoslovak territory to Germany in 1938 under a failed policy of appeasement.
Germany and the Soviet Union signed the German-Soviet Nonaggression Pact in August 1939 to divide Poland.
German forces invaded Poland on September 1, 1939, starting the war in Europe.
Great Britain and France declared war on Germany on September 3, 1939.
Soviet troops invaded eastern Poland on September 17, 1939, fulfilling terms of the secret protocol.
The Soviet victory at the Battle of Stalingrad in February 1943 shattered the German eastern offensive.
Allied armies advanced into western Germany while Soviet troops captured Berlin in May 1945.
Adolf Hitler committed suicide in his Berlin bunker on April 30, 1945.
Germany signed an unconditional surrender at Reims, France, on May 7, 1945, taking effect May 8.
Allied leaders issued the Potsdam Declaration on July 26, 1945, demanding Japan surrender unconditionally.
The United States dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima on August 6 and Nagasaki on August 9, 1945.
The Soviet Union declared war on Japan and invaded Japanese-occupied Manchuria on August 9, 1945.
Japan formally signed surrender documents aboard the battleship USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay on September 2, 1945.
